title: Indoor Air Quality & Comfort Anomaly Detection

blueprintSignals.name: CO2 vs occupancy
blueprintSignals.definition: residual between measured CO2 and the CO2 expected for the current occupancy
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Occupancy counts are noisy, so smooth them

blueprintSignals.name: Humidity drift
blueprintSignals.definition: slope of relative humidity over 7 days with a seasonal baseline
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Seasonal effects are strong, so compare with the same season

blueprintSignals.name: Particulate spike
blueprintSignals.definition: PM2.5 rise above the rolling baseline, compared with outdoor PM2.5
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Outdoor pollution enters, so compare with outside

blueprintSignals.name: Temperature gradient
blueprintSignals.definition: difference in temperature between adjacent zones and between floor and ceiling sensors

engineFeatures.meaning: value minus the median of the same hour of the same weekday in previous weeks
median absolute deviation of recent residuals
known events that are supposed to move the level
persistence of a deviation over several hours
quiet time after an alert so one event raises one alert

label: For "Indoor Air Quality & Comfort Anomaly Detection": Detect abnormal CO2, humidity, temperature and particulate readings so facilities fix ventilation and comfort issues. Define the label exactly as in milestone M1: what counts as a positive or a correct outcome, and when it becomes known. Design around this trap first: Few labelled events, so recall is poorly estimated.
